items.title: Modular diagnostic stack: layered architecture (hardware → transport → protocol → application) with standard library reuse

model_routing.scope: Cross-layer contracts and transport migration need senior ownership; no broad junior rewrite or unapproved DoIP/BLE expansion.

items.notes: 2026-11-04 status reconciliation: joint request/target/result/origin design accepted; P01-P04 policy and CAN/J2534/ELM/simulation repairs plus P11 integration accepted. This is substantial groundwork, not completion of every proposed v1 schema, legacy migration or module extraction. K-line timing is preserved; DoIP/TP2.0/BLE/newer-platform expansion remains deferred. Source qualifiers govern protocol selection: selected WP12 CAN links use KWP2000 over ISO-TP, not automatic UDS or TP2.0. No real987/OBDLink acceptance. Latest recorded DEV23d6024 is deployed with optional local login; actual laptop installation/normal-helper/public-page no-cable onboarding accepted under the later30000 ceiling. Physical driver/car acceptance remains separate. See docs/plans/FRONTIER_REMEDIATION_2026-11-02.yaml and TEST_LAPTOP.md. HISTORICAL DESIGN WISHLIST below is not implemented capability or byte authority; the joint DIAG_STACK_ARCHITECTURE.md contract supersedes it. Goal: make the diagnostic stack modular, expandable, easy to understand, KISS. Reuse good existing libraries; do not reinvent. Current state: bespoke K-Line code in tools/kline_probe.py + helper/openpiwis_helper/ handles KWP2000 (ISO 14230) over serial, ISO 9141 5-baud init, OBD-II modes, and Porsche-specific services (0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x17, 0x18, 0x19, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x27, 0x3E, 0x2E, 0x30, 0x31, 0x32). CAN/UDS + DoIP support is the open gap (987/997 parked for car testing; 9x1/G1/992 extracted 2026-10-29; 992 confirmed UDS-on-DoIP, 9x1/G1 all-CAN per comms). Target architecture: 4 layers. LAYER 1 - HARDWARE (extract): K-Line serial (FTDI/D2XX/pyserial) from gkbus KLineHardware + bespoke FTDI/D2XX glue. CAN bus from python-can (industry standard, BSD-3, many backends: SocketCAN, PCAN, Kvaser, Vector). Ethernet/DoIP hardware: OBD2->RJ45 passive cable (ISO 13400-4 Option 1, OBD pins 3/11/12/13 + pin 8) or VAS 6154 (192.168.1.69:13400) - 992 ODX confirms DoIP on the OBD port (VCONN_DoIP_Diagnose, pins 12 TX+ / 3 RX+). LAYER 2 - TRANSPORT (extract): K-Line (ISO 9141) from KWP2000-CAN kline.py. ISO-TP (ISO 15765-2) from python-can-isotp (MIT, mature, well-tested). TP20 (VAG) from KWP2000-CAN can.py. DoIP (ISO 13400-2) from python-doipclient (jacobschaer, MIT; vehicle identification/announcement UDP 13400 + routing activation + TCP diagnostic) - NEW 2026-10-29, transport for 992 (confirmed) and the other DoIP platforms. LAYER 3 - PROTOCOL (extract + bespoke): KWP2000 (ISO 14230) from gkbus kwp2000.py + KWP2000-CAN. UDS (ISO 14229) from udsoncan (MIT, extensive docs, active community) or py-uds (MIT, multi-bus, client+server, error injection). OBD-II from python-obd (BSD-3, ELM327) + bespoke K-line OBD. LAYER 4 - APPLICATION (bespoke, per-generation): Porsche-specific services. 986/996 (K-Line): DTC read/clear (0x14, 0x17, 0x18 with groupOfDTC), freeze frames (0x12), ECU ident (0x1A), memory read (0x23), coding (0x22, 0x2E), actuator tests (0x30, 0x31, 0x32), security access (0x27), TesterPresent (0x3E). 987/997 (CAN/UDS): same services via UDS 0x10, 0x19, 0x1A, 0x22, 0x23, 0x3E + KWP2000 over CAN (TP20) for pre-UDS modules. 981/718 (CAN/UDS): same stack, different ECU addresses + service sets. PHASE 1 (986/996 K-Line, improve existing): Extract hardware abstraction from gkbus. Extract KWP2000 command/response pattern from gkbus. Extract SecurityAccess (0x27) implementation from gkbus. Keep bespoke K-Line timing + Porsche-specific services. Add OBD-II command tables from python-obd. PHASE 2 (987/997 CAN/UDS, new head start): Add python-can as CAN transport. Add python-can-isotp as ISO-TP transport. Add udsoncan (or py-uds) as UDS application layer. Extract KWP2000 over CAN (TP20) from KWP2000-CAN. Write Porsche-specific application layer (ECU addresses from WP12, service sets, coding, actuator tests). Enforce read-only allow-list (AGENTS.md rule 1). PHASE 3 (981/718, future): Reuse same CAN/UDS stack. Add 981/718-specific ECU address tables + service sets. Transport layer shared across all generations. KEY PRINCIPLES: KISS - reuse good existing code, do not reinvent. Layering - each layer depends only on the one below. Expandable - adding a new generation = new application layer, same transport/protocol. Easy to understand - clean separation, standard library names, minimal bespoke code. Libraries researched 2026-10-28: KWP2000-CAN (EliasTuning, MIT, KWP2000 over CAN+K-Line, TP20, DS2, 6 stars, Dec 2025), gkbus (KWP2000 over CAN+K-Line, CCP, SecurityAccess, v0.4.90, Oct 2026), openobd (Jifeline, commercial, ISO 14230 K-line, TP2.0, DoIP, OBD, v1.26.11, Sep 2026), python-obd (BSD-3, OBD-II, ELM327, <1.0.0), py-uds (MIT, UDS multi-bus, client+server, error injection, Python 3.12+, K-Line planned), python-can-isotp (MIT, ISO-TP, python-can integration, v2.x, 199 commits), python-can (BSD-3, CAN bus, industry standard), udsoncan (MIT, UDS, CAN, extensive docs, active community), python-doipclient (jacobschaer, MIT, DoIP ISO 13400-2, vehicle identification + routing activation + diagnostic, researched 2026-10-29). Deliverables: (1) Architecture document in docs/specs/ describing the 4-layer design with library choices + rationale. (2) Refactored helper/openpiwis_helper/ with clean layer separation. (3) New CAN/UDS transport + protocol modules for 987/997. (4) Updated tools/kline_probe.py to use the new layered stack. (5) Tests for each layer. (6) Updated AGENTS.md + README.md with the new architecture. (7) Updated docs/features.yaml + docs/STATUS.md. Acceptance: python tools/run_all_tests.py passes. 986/996 K-Line still works (replay tests pass). 987/997 CAN/UDS stack is in place and ready for first car contact. Architecture is documented and easy to understand. No bespoke code where a standard library already exists. NEW LEARNINGS 2026-10-29 (DoIP/Ethernet + cable matrix): (1) 992 first extracted platform with UDS-on-DoIP (9 links) + OBD; ODX puts DoIP on the OBD port (pins 12/3, ISO 13400-4 Option 1) so an E-NET-style passive OBD2->RJ45 cable should physically work (pin-8 activation + minus-pair UNCONFIRMED from ODX - verify on a real car). (2) DoIP CONFIRMED only on 992; 9x1/G1 have DoIP .pr.db files but 0 LL refs (all CAN) - DoIP need UNCONFIRMED. (3) Cable/adapter inventory + platform->transport matrix captured in docs/ROADMAP.md (Hardware & cable support) + task R-CABLE-KNOWLEDGE (handoff docs/HANDOFF_CABLE_KNOWLEDGE.md -> docs/hardware/CABLES_AND_ADAPTERS.md); treat cable/adapter as first-class Layer-1 concern (profile-driven, helper/openpiwis_helper/profiles/). (4) PO42X adds CAN-FD (ISO 11898-1:2015) on top of DoIP - transport must be CAN-FD-ready. (5) Existing DoIP code: helper/openpiwis_helper/transport.py NetworkVCITransport (routing activation + 0x8001 frames, VAS 6154) - review/replace with python-doipclient in the refactor. (6) DEMO MODE VIRTUAL TRANSPORT INTEGRATION (INTERTWINED WITH I-DEMO-VIRTUAL-INTERFACE): The modular architecture must natively accommodate both physical hardware adapters (FTDI K-Line, python-can, ISO-TP, DoIP) and virtual/simulated buses. Rather than treating Demo Mode as special UI logic with mock branches, the stack's Layer 1 (Hardware) / Layer 2 (Transport) will support a `VirtualBusTransport` / simulation provider that replays realistic vehicle frames, timings, and error states from vehicle/scenario models. Application (Layer 4) and Protocol (Layer 3) remain 100% identical between live and simulated sessions.
